method: All conversion arithmetic uses ingredient mass. Let F be the fresh-yeast-equivalent mass. For a fresh input F equals the input mass; for active dry input F equals input mass divided by 0.4; for instant input F equals input mass divided by 0.33. The three outputs are F, 0.4F and 0.33F respectively. These are the general conversion multipliers published by King Arthur Baking, not a universal manufacturer specification. Inputs allow 0.1–1000 grams, 0.01–35 avoirdupois ounces, 0.1–300 teaspoons or 0.1–100 standard packets, with at most four decimal places. Fresh yeast accepts grams or ounces only because no standard fresh-yeast teaspoon or packet volume is assumed. One ounce is exactly 28.349523125 grams. Dry-yeast teaspoons and packets are approximate and use Red Star’s convention that one standard 7-gram packet contains about 2.25 teaspoons. Conversion factors and unrounded values are retained throughout the core; the interface rounds gram, teaspoon and packet displays to two decimal places and ounce displays to three. The tool converts ingredient quantity only. It does not prescribe fermentation time, liquid adjustments, bread-machine settings, viability, storage or food-safety handling. Manufacturer instructions and the recipe take precedence where their substitution ratios differ.
